1) a rule-based approach is useful for studying multivalent ligand binding to cell surface receptors, and 2) steric constraints on ligand-receptor configurations may play a key role in regulating ligand-induced receptor clustering and the kinetics of cellular responses.

1) flow cytometry can be used to characterize the kinetics of ligandreceptor interactions in which the receptor is a multivalent cell-surface protein; 2) steric effects that limit ligand-induced receptor aggregate formation may be important; and 3) transient formation of small cyclic receptor aggregates may be important.
